Title: Rapid binge-like eating and body weight gain driven by zona incerta GABA neuron activation.
Authors: Zhang X, van den Pol AN

Authors and Publication Year: Xiaobing Zhang; Anthony N. van den Pol; 2017
Anatomical connections: ZI (VGAT+) → PVT (vGlut2+) (anterograde AAV-ChIEF-tdTomato); PVT (vGlut2+) ← ZI (VGAT+) (monosynaptic rabies-EnvA-ΔG); PSTh (vGlut2+) → PVT (vGlut2+) (monosynaptic rabies-EnvA-ΔG; anterograde AAV-ChIEF-tdTomato)

Title: Bidirectional modulation of accumbens dopamine by MCH neurons during learning and consummatory behavior.
Authors: Potter LE, Toth BA, Manna J, Lyons HC, Evans JR, Burgess CR
Animal Model: MCH-Cre (Strain#014099) mice, littermate controls, and Pmch∆Vglut2 mice (Pmch-iCre × Slc17a6tm1Lowl/J, JAX® #012898)

Title: Systematic Input-Output Mapping Reveals Structural Plasticity of VTA Dopamine Neurons-Zona Incerta Loop Underlying the Social Buffering Effects in Learned Helplessness.
Authors: Cai H, Zhang P, Qi G, Zhang L, Li T, Li M, Lv X, Lei J, Ming J, Tian B

Authors and Publication Year: Hongwei Cai; Pei Zhang; Guangjian Qi; Lijun Zhang; Tongxia Li; Ming Li; Xinyuan Lv; Jie Lei; Jie Ming; Bo Tian; 2022
Anatomical connections:
Retrograde monosynaptic rabies tracing: Inputs to TH+ VTA dopamine neurons from central amygdala (CEA), nucleus accumbens (ACB), anterior amygdalar area (AAA), substantia innominata (SI), bed nuclei of stria terminalis (BST), lateral hypothalamic area (LHA), zona incerta (ZI), pontine central gray (PCG), periaqueductal gray (PAG), parabrachial nucleus (PB), substantia nigra reticulata (SNr). Helper viruses AAV9-TH-Cre + AAV9-DIO-TVA-His-EYFP + AAV9-DIO-RG injected (150 nl total volume) into VTA (AP +1.24 mm, ML ±0.6 mm, DV +4.6 mm), followed 33 days later by EnVA-RV-ΔG-dsRed (150 nl), survival 7 days, N = 4 (CON), 6 (LH), 4 (LH+SB); quantification: percent of dsRed+ cells normalized to starter cells.
Anterograde AAV tracing: Outputs from TH+ VTA dopamine neurons to caudoputamen (CP), nucleus accumbens (ACB), olfactory tubercle (OT), medial septum (MS), substantia innominata (SI), nucleus of reuniens (RE), retrosplenial area ventral (RSPv), lateral habenula (LHb), posterior hypothalamus (PH), parasubthalamic nucleus (PSTN), ZI, PCG, SNr, PAG, raphe magnus (RM), inferior olivary complex (IO). AAV9-TH-Cre + AAV9-DIO-ChR2-EYFP injected (150 nl total volume) into VTA (same coordinates), survival 21 days, N = 5 (CON), 4 (LH), 4 (LH+SB); quantification: axon pixel density normalized to total signal.
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological verification via fluorescent imaging of 40 μm coronal sections at ZI levels (bregma −0.4 mm and −1.7 mm), comparison to Allen Mouse Brain Atlas landmarks
Purpose of this circuit: To reveal the structural plasticity of the VTA dopamine neuron–ZI loop that underlies social buffering in learned helplessness

Title: Chemogenetic and optogenetic stimulation of zona incerta GABAergic neurons ameliorates motor impairment in Parkinson's disease.

Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological verification via immunofluorescence staining of cannula location and virus expression in ZI GABAergic neurons
Purpose of this circuit: To determine whether and how ZI GABAergic neuron activity regulates motor behaviors in a Parkinson’s disease mouse model

Title: Prefrontal - subthalamic pathway supports action selection in a spatial working memory task.
Authors: Heikenfeld C, Mederos S, Chen C, Korotkova T, Schnitzler A, Ponomarenko A
Animal Model: Wild-type C57BL/6 mice (12–25 weeks old)
Authors and Publication Year: Carla Heikenfeld, Sara Mederos, Changwan Chen, Tatiana Korotkova, Alfons Schnitzler & Alexey Ponomarenko (2020)
Anatomical connections: Anterograde AAV-hSyn-eNPAC2.0-EYFP tracing: mPFC→ventromedial STN and mPFC→ZI (injection in mPFC at AP:1.5, ML:±0.2, DV:3.1–3.3 mm; 250 nl at 200 nl/min; N=3 mice).
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Confocal fluorescence imaging of EYFP-labeled mPFC fibers confirming arborization in ZI (Fig. 1A).
Purpose of this circuit: Supports action selection during spatial working memory by theta-rhythmic coordination of gamma oscillations in the prefrontal-subthalamic pathway.

Title: Modulation of fear generalization by the zona incerta.
Authors: Venkataraman A, Brody N, Reddi P, Guo J, Gordon Rainnie D, Dias BG
Animal Model: Adult female and male C57BL/6J (wild-type) and vGAT-Cre transgenic mice
Authors and Publication Year: Archana Venkataraman; Natalia Brody; Preethi Reddi; Jidong Guo; Donald Gordon Rainnie; Brian George Dias (2019)
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Post-mortem histological verification of viral injection sites via fluorescent reporter (mCherry) and Hoechst nuclear staining under fluorescence microscopy
Purpose of this circuit: To test whether the zona incerta modulates fear generalization and to evaluate its potential as a therapeutic target to reduce maladaptive fear generalization.

Title: Activity of GABA neurons in the zona incerta and ventral lateral periaqueductal grey is biased towards sleep.
Authors: Blanco-Centurion C, Vidal-Ortiz A, Sato T, Shiromani PJ
Animal Model: vGAT‐ires‐Cre mice (Jackson Laboratories, JAX stock #016962), adult (6.2 ± 0.3 mo) mice
Authors and Publication Year: Carlos Blanco‐Centurion; Aurelio Vidal‐Ortiz; Takashi Sato; Priyattam J. Shiromani; 2023
Anatomical connections: vGAT+ ZI → vlPAG projection (anterograde): rAAV5-hSyn-Flex-ChrimsonR-tdT expressed in ZI GABA neurons; ZI injection coordinates AP −1.6 mm, ML 0.8 mm, DV −4.5 mm; vlPAG injection coordinates AP −4.3 mm, ML 0.9 mm, DV −2.2 mm
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological confirmation of GRIN lens placement and GCaMP6M+ cell bodies within anatomical ZI boundaries, as shown in Figure 1
Photometry Data: ZI vGAT neurons (rAAV-DJ-EF1α-DIO-GCaMP6M; Inscopix miniscope, GRIN lens): n=11 mice, 682 neurons; classified by state with abundances: R-Max 51.03%, W-Max 23.9%, NR-Max 11.7%, W/R-Max 6.5%, No Change 6.9%. vlPAG vGAT neurons: n=5 mice, 169 neurons; classified: R-Max 60.95%, W-Max 25.44%, R-OFF 8.28%, W/R-Max 2.96%, No Change 2.37%; states aligned to Active Wake, Quiet Wake, NREM, REM transition, REM sleep
Purpose of this circuit: To characterize the in vivo activity patterns of GABAergic neurons in the ZI and vlPAG across sleep–wake states to determine their bias toward sleep and identify sleep‐promoting roles.

Title: The zona incerta negatively regulates the red nucleus during movement cued by sound signals.
Authors: Chen L, Wang X, Liu H, He C, Chen APF, Chen L, Kim TA, Xiong Q
Animal Model: Mus musculus: C57BL/6J wild-type; PV-Cre, SOM-Cre, Lhx6-Cre, GAD-Cre, VGlut2-Cre transgenic mouse lines
Authors and Publication Year: Liang Chen, Xinxing Wang, Hanxiao Liu, Chenzhao He, Allen P. F. Chen, Lu Chen, Thomas A. Kim, Qiaojie Xiong; 2025
Anatomical connections: 1) Monosynaptic retrograde rabies tracing from RN excitatory neurons in VGlut2-Cre mice (AAV-FLEX-TVA-oG + EnvA-G-deleted Rabies-mCherry) revealed direct inputs from motor cortex (M1, M2), cingulate cortex (Cg1), somatosensory cortex (S1), subthalamic nucleus (STN), substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNr), and ventral medial ZI (vZIm) to ipsilateral RN. 2) Cre-dependent anterograde AAV-DIO-GFP tracing in PV-Cre mice injected into ZI (2.0 mm caudal, 1.6 mm lateral, 4.0 mm depth) demonstrated PV+ ZI neurons project densely to ipsilateral RN (3.6 mm caudal, 0.6 mm lateral, 3.5 mm depth).
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological confirmation via immunostaining of GFP-expressing neurons and interneuron marker staining (PV, Lhx6, SST) in medial ZI, and post hoc DiI labeling of tetrode and fiber tracks in ventral medial ZI (vZIm).
Purpose of this circuit: To provide an inhibitory ZI-RN pathway that shapes auditory-cued goal-directed movement by modulating contralateral movement choices.

Title: Divergent BLA engram circuits orchestrate social preference dynamics in bystander male mice with self-experienced stress.
Authors: Yang XK, Shi YL, Li M, Li TX, Yang J, Lei J, Cui C, Peng X, Zha HC, Luo GG, Yao YB, Chen ST, Du JS, Wang HJ, Xu SQ, Zhang P, Tian B
Animal Model: C57BL/6J male mice (experimental); CD1 outbred male mice (aggressors)
Authors and Publication Year: Xue-Ke Yang, Yu-Long Shi, Ming Li, Tong-Xia Li, Jian Yang, Jie Lei, Chi Cui, Xiang Peng, Hong-Chu Zha, Gan-Gan Luo, Yi-Bo Yao, Si-Tong Chen, Jun-Song Du, Hui-Juan Wang, Shi-Qi Xu, Pei Zhang, and Bo Tian; 2026
Anatomical connections: BLA engram cells → ACC (anterograde; AAV2/9-c-fos-tTA + TRE-EYFP)  |  ACCGlu neurons ← BLAEC (monosynaptic retrograde; RV-EnvA-ΔG-DsRed)  |  ACCGlu neurons → dorsal hippocampus (anterograde; AAV1-CaMKII-Cre + DIO-mCherry)  |  ACCGlu neurons → ventral hippocampus (same)  |  ACCGlu neurons → zona incerta (same)
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological verification via fluorescence imaging of mCherry-labeled ACC terminals and fiber placement in ZI; no subregional specification
Photometry Data: Population: SSDS-labeled BLA engram cells expressing GCaMP (AAV2/9-DIO-GCaMP); recorded via fiber photometry. Behavioral epochs: entry into novelty vs. cagemate chamber during SPT; entry into interaction zone during SAT. SSDS+VSDS mice show increased Ca²⁺ signal (peak ΔF/F, AUC, total z-score) in cagemate chamber and interaction zone relative to SSDS+CON controls; N = 8 mice per group.
Electrophysiology Data: In vivo extracellular single-unit recordings in ACC during optogenetic activation (473 nm) and inhibition (590 nm) of BLAEC-ACC projections; measured firing rate changes but no whole-cell parameters (Cm, Rin) reported.
Purpose of this circuit: To orchestrate social preference dynamics—promoting interaction with defeat-experienced cagemates and avoidance of aggressors—via divergent BLA engram cell circuits.

Title: Parvalbumin Neurons in Zona Incerta Regulate Itch in Mice.
Authors: Li J, Bai Y, Liang Y, Zhang Y, Zhao Q, Ge J, Li D, Zhu Y, Cai G, Tao H, Wu S, Huang J
Animal Model: Adult male C57BL/6J mice and PV-IRES-Cre (PV-Cre) mice on a C57BL/6J background
Authors and Publication Year: Li J; Bai Y; Liang Y; Zhang Y; Zhao Q; Ge J; Li D; Zhu Y; Cai G; Tao H; Wu S; Huang J (2022)
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological verification of viral expression and fiber placement in ZI via immunofluorescent staining of viral reporter and PV, confirmed with atlas-guided confocal imaging
Photometry Data: Three recordings of ZI PV neuron bulk calcium signals via fiber photometry of GCaMP6s in PV-Cre mice: 1) Histamine-induced acute itch: ΔF/F increase onset 0.10±2.45 s to duration 5.13±1.57 s post-scratching (n=6 GCaMP, n=5 EYFP; repeated-measures ANOVA AUC F(1,9)=27.892, P=0.001; permutation test P<0.05). 2) Chloroquine-induced acute itch: onset 0.16±0.28 s to duration 4.08±0.71 s (n=6, n=5; F(1,9)=36.586, P<0.001). 3) Chronic AD itch: onset 0.78±0.18 s to duration 7.36±1.42 s (n=6, n=4; F(1,8)=14.355, P<0.01). Controls expressed EYFP; recording system ThinkerTech fiber photometry.
Purpose of this circuit: ZI PV neurons function as an endogenous negative modulator of itch processing, suppressing scratching behavior.

Title: Zona incerta modulation of the inferior olive and the pontine nuclei.
Authors: Bhuvanasundaram R, Washburn S, Krzyspiak J, Khodakhah K
Animal Model: C57BL/6 wild-type mice (both sexes); 7–10 weeks old for in vivo; 5–6 weeks old juvenile for in vitro slices
Authors and Publication Year: Ramakrishnan Bhuvanasundaram; Samantha Washburn; Joanna Krzyspiak; Kamran Khodakhah, 2024
Anatomical connections: Anterograde AAV2-hSyn-ChR2-YFP tracing from ZI (center; Bregma −2.1 mm AP, ±1.5 mm ML, −4 mm DV; 0.25/0.15 μl at 0.1 μl/min; hSyn promoter; survival ≥2 weeks) to pontine nuclei; Anterograde AAV2-hSyn-ChR2-YFP tracing from ZI to inferior olive
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Post-hoc immunohistochemical verification of ChR2-YFP expression confined to ZI; injection centered in ZI; exclusion of cases with spread beyond ZI
Purpose of this circuit: These ZI→PN and ZI→IO pathways may modulate the cerebellar network and underlie the efficacy of ZI deep brain stimulation in tremor-related movement disorders.

Title: A hypoxia-sensitive medullary nucleus modulates cerebral blood flow via a disynaptic pathway to cortex.
Authors: Chhabria K, Duckworth J, Yao P, Fassihi-Zakeri A, Kleinfeld D
Animal Model: Dβh-Cre transgenic mice on C57BL/6J background; B6.Cg-Tg(Acta2-GCaMP8.1/mVermilion) for smooth muscle–specific GCaMP8.1
Authors and Publication Year: Karishma Chhabria, Jacob Duckworth, Pantong Yao, Arash Fassihi-Zakeri, David Kleinfeld; 2026
Anatomical connections: RVLMDβh —anterograde AAV-Flex-mCherry→ LH; RVLMDβh —anterograde AAV-Flex-mCherry→ ZI; RVLMDβh —anterograde AAV-Flex-mCherry→ LC, PAG/DR, PBN/Tg; RVLMDβh —transsynaptic HSV-H129→ layer V cortex via LH/ZI (disynaptic); RVLMDβh —transsynaptic HSV-H129→ layer V cortex via LC (disynaptic)
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Anterograde AAV-Flex-mCherry labeling in Dβh-Cre mice with histological verification via TH immunostaining; ZI identified by fiber labeling in coronal sections
Photometry Data: Population: RVLMDβh neurons; Indicator: GCaMP8s via AAV-Flex-jGCaMP8s fiber photometry; Epoch: baseline vs. hypoxia (<16% O2) vs. recovery; Mean ΔF/F: no change; RMS ΔF/F: increased during hypoxia (p=0.019, n=7 mice); N animals=7; N trials not stated; Calcium leads CBF by ~2 s; Statistical test: Wilcoxon; Figure 1F–I
Purpose of this circuit: To provide an adaptive, hypoxia-sensitive pathway from RVLM to cortex that rapidly increases cerebral blood flow across the cortical mantle

Title: A GABAergic Projection from the Zona Incerta to the Rostral Ventromedial Medulla Modulates Descending Control of Neuropathic Pain.
Authors: Zou L, Ding H, Hu Y, Wen Z, Yu L, Yan M
Animal Model: Wild-type C57BL/6J and Vgat-Cre transgenic male mice, 6–8 weeks old
Authors and Publication Year: Lijing Zou; Hao Ding; Yujiao Hu; Zhuo Wen; Lina Yu; Min Yan, 2026
Anatomical connections: ZI GABAergic (Vgat+) neurons → ipsilateral RVM (anterograde tracing with AAV2/9-hSyn-DIO-EGFP in Vgat-Cre mice; monosynaptic anterograde tracing with scAAV2/1-hSyn-Cre in ZI and AAV2/9-hSyn-DIO-mCherry in RVM)
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological confirmation of viral expression in ZI via EGFP/mCherry fluorescence at coordinates AP +2.15 mm, ML ±1.65 mm, DV −4.00 mm

Title: [Activation of GABAergic neurons in the zona incerta accelerates anesthesia induction with sevoflurane and propofol without affecting anesthesia maintenance or awakening in mice].
Authors: Cao F, Guo Y, Guo S, Zhou Z, Cao J, Tong L, Mi W
Animal Model: Male C57BL/6J mice (8–10 weeks old, 20–23 g)
Authors and Publication Year: Cao Fuyang; Guo Yongxin; Guo Shuting; Zhou Zhikang; Cao Jiangbei; Tong Li; Mi Weidong; 2023
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Immunofluorescent histological verification of viral expression in ZI by co-labeling mCherry/GFP with GABA and c-Fos antibodies (with DAPI), and confirmation of correct stereotaxic injection coordinates and placement of EEG electrodes and optical fiber.
Purpose of this circuit: To explore the regulatory effects of ZI GABAergic neurons on the induction and emergence of sevoflurane and propofol anesthesia.

Title: Paradoxical effects of posterior intralaminar thalamic calretinin neurons on hippocampal seizure via distinct downstream circuits.
Authors: Qi Y, Cheng H, Lou Q, Wang X, Lai N, Gao C, Wu S, Xu C, Ruan Y, Chen Z, Wang Y
Animal Model: B6(Cg)-Calb2tm1(cre)Zjh (CR-cre) mice and C57BL/6J mice
Authors and Publication Year: Yingbei Qi, Heming Cheng, Qiuwen Lou, Xia Wang, Nanxi Lai, Chenshu Gao, Shuangshuang Wu, Cenglin Xu, Yeping Ruan, Zhong Chen, Yi Wang; 2022
Anatomical connections: Anterograde AAV2/9-CAG-FLEX-ArchT-GFP tracing from PIL CR neurons (injections at AP –3.1 mm, ML 1.7 mm, DV 3.6 mm; 0.5 µl at 0.1 µl/min; 5 weeks expression) revealed projections from PIL to lateral amygdala (LA), zona incerta (ZI), auditory cortex (Au), and central amygdaloid nucleus (CeA). Retrograde AAV2/2Retro-hEF1a-DIO-eYFP from LA and AAV2/2Retro-hEF1a-DIO-mCherry from ZI labeled LA- and ZI-projecting CR neurons in PIL with partial overlap (~42.7% of ZI-projecting and ~70.4% of LA-projecting neurons).
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological confirmation of ArchT-GFP expression and optic fiber placement in the ZI via GFP immunofluorescence and imaging of Arch-GFP axon fibers in ZI
Photometry Data: Population: PIL CR neurons expressing GCaMP6s via AAV2/9-Ef1a-DIO-GCaMP6s in CR-cre mice, recorded by fiber photometry (488 nm laser, PMT, 200 µm fiber). During focal seizures (FS), Ca2+ activity showed a slight increase relative to baseline (n=6 mice, 12 trials; Wilcoxon test, p<0.01; Figure 1E–G). During generalized seizures (GS), Ca2+ activity increased during latency and further increased at seizure onset (n=6 mice, 12 trials; Friedman test, p<0.0001; Figure 1I–K).
Purpose of this circuit: To determine how posterior intralaminar thalamic calretinin neuron circuits modulate hippocampal seizure progression via distinct downstream pathways.

Title: Glutamatergic Neurons in the Zona Incerta Modulate Pain and Itch Behaviors in Mice.
Authors: Li J, Peng S, Zhang Y, Ge J, Gao S, Zhu Y, Bai Y, Wu S, Huang J
Animal Model: Adult male C57BL/6J mice and VGluT2-IRES-Cre mice
Authors and Publication Year: Jiaqi Li; Shihao Peng; Yiwen Zhang; Junye Ge; Shasha Gao; Yuanyuan Zhu; Yang Bai; Shengxi Wu; Jing Huang (2023)
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological verification of viral expression and fiber placement in caudal ZI by confocal imaging and DAPI; FOS immunostaining of hM3Dq-expressing neurons; atlas-based segmentation using Photoshop and Paxinos & Franklin atlas
Photometry Data:
Population: ZI VGluT2 neurons (GCaMP6s in VGluT2-Cre mice; fiber photometry)
Epoch 1: Mechanical nocifensive withdrawal (von Frey, 1 g); ΔF/F increased; AUC pre vs. post, P=0.033; n=7 mice
Epoch 2: Thermal nocifensive withdrawal (heat beam, 30 °C); ΔF/F increased; P=0.021; n=6 mice
Epoch 3: Histamine-induced scratching; ΔF/F increased at scratching onset; Friedman’s M test, P=0.346; n=9 mice
Epoch 4: Chloroquine-induced scratching; ΔF/F increased at scratching onset; Friedman's M test, P=0.134; n=8 mice
Purpose of this circuit: To act as an endogenous negative modulatory center suppressing pain and itch behaviors

Title: Raphe serotonin projections dynamically regulate feeding behavior through targeting inhibitory circuits from rostral zona incerta to paraventricular thalamus.
Authors: Ye Q, Nunez J, Zhang X
Animal Model: C57BL/6J mice, Sert-Cre mice, vGAT-Cre mice, GAD67-GFP mice
Authors and Publication Year: Qiying Ye, Jeremiah Nunez, Xiaobing Zhang; 2022
Anatomical connections:
- DR/MnR 5-HT neurons → rostral zona incerta (ZIR) (anterograde AAV1-FLEX-EGFP-WPRE in Sert-Cre mice)
- DR/MnR 5-HT neurons → paraventricular thalamus (PVT) (anterograde AAV1-FLEX-EGFP-WPRE in Sert-Cre mice)
- DR/MnR 5-HT neurons → ZIR & PVT (retrograde AAVrg-CAG-FLEX-EGFP in ZIR and AAVrg-CAG-FLEX-tdTomato in PVT showing collateralization in Sert-Cre mice)
- ZIR GABA neurons → PVT (retrograde CTB-555 tracing in GAD-GFP mice)
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological confirmation of viral expression and fiber placement within rostral ZI using fluorescent reporter imaging and reference to Allen Mouse Brain Atlas
Purpose of this circuit: To elucidate how raphe serotonin projections modulate the inhibitory ZIR → PVT pathway to regulate feeding motivation and food intake.

Title: Somatostatin-Positive Neurons in the Rostral Zona Incerta Modulate Innate Fear-Induced Defensive Response in Mice.
Authors: Lin S, Zhu MY, Tang MY, Wang M, Yu XD, Zhu Y, Xie SZ, Yang D, Chen J, Li XM
Animal Model: Adult (>8 weeks old) male SST-Cre (SST-IRES-Cre) and Ai14 transgenic mice (Mus musculus)
Authors and Publication Year: Shan Lin, Meng-Yue Zhu, Meng-Yu Tang, Mi Wang, Xiao-Dan Yu, Yi Zhu, Shi-Ze Xie, Dan Yang, Jiadong Chen, Xiao-Ming Li; 2022
Anatomical connections:
• Rostral ZI SST-positive → nucleus reuniens (Re): Anterograde AAV2/9-DIO-mGFP-Synaptophysin-mRuby injection into rostral ZI SST-Cre mice (70 nL); reporter expression in Re; functional GABAergic projection confirmed ex vivo by optogenetically-evoked IPSCs in Re neurons.
• Superior colliculus → rostral ZI SST-positive: Monosynaptic rabies tracing via AAV2/9-DIO-TVA-EGFP and AAV2/9-EF1α-DIO-RVG in rostral ZI followed by RV-EnvA-ΔG-dsRed into rostral ZI (80 nL); labeled neurons in intermediate and deep layers of SC.
• SC → rostral ZI SST-positive → Re (SC-ZIrSST-Re tri-synaptic): Monosynaptic rabies from Re in ZI TVA/RVG-preinfected SST-Cre mice, combined with c-Fos staining after looming; identified SC neurons projecting to Re-projecting ZI SST cells that were activated by looming.
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological verification by fluorescence microscopy showing Cre-dependent reporter expression and fiber tracks in the rostral ZI (AP −1.00 mm; ML ±0.6–1.35 mm; DV −4.45 to −4.13 mm) with DAPI counterstaining; RNAscope in situ hybridization confirming SST mRNA expression in SST-positive neurons.
Photometry Data: Population of SST-positive neurons in the rostral ZI recorded with AAV2/9-DIO-GCaMP6s (fiber photometry). Looming stimulus (3 expanding disks over 3 s) evoked a significant increase in ΔF/F% (AUC difference p=0.0313; n=6 mice, 3 trials each); sweeping stimulus elicited intracellular Ca2+ elevation; spontaneous locomotion produced no change. mCherry control channel showed no signal changes.
Electrophysiology Data:
1) ChR2 in rostral ZI SST neurons: 20 Hz, 10 ms blue light pulses reliably evoked action potentials in current-clamp.
2) GtACR1 in rostral ZI SST neurons: 5 s continuous 473 nm light induced hyperpolarization and silenced firing.
3) ZIrSST→Re synaptic connectivity: optogenetic stimulation of ZI SST axon terminals evoked monosynaptic GABAergic IPSCs in Re neurons (blocked by TTX, rescued by 4-AP; abolished by picrotoxin). No measurements of Cm, Rin, AP kinetics, or resting membrane potential were reported.
Purpose of this circuit: To mediate and modulate innate visual threat-induced defensive behaviors (flight and freezing) via SST-positive neurons in the rostral ZI and the SC-ZIrSST-Re tri-synaptic circuit.

Title: The zona incerta regulates burying behavior and normalizes anxiety-like behavior in inescapable stressful male mice by object cue.
Authors: Liu Y, Qiu L, Qian J, Xu Q, Qi R, Luo Y, Cao Z, Zhang Z, Wu W, Zhang L, Lu G
Animal Model: Male C57BL/6J mice
Authors and Publication Year: Yueqin Liu; Lianli Qiu; Jiahui Qian; Qiang Xu; Rongfeng Qi; Yifeng Luo; Zhihong Cao; Zhiqiang Zhang; Wei Wu; Longjiang Zhang; Guangming Lu (2025)
Anatomical connections: 1) ZI→vPAG, anterograde tracing: rAAV-hSyn-EYFP injected into ZI at AP −1.2 mm, ML ±1.6 mm, DV 4.4 mm; abundant EYFP+ fibers observed in vPAG. 2) ZI→vPAG, retrograde-based intersectional labeling: AAV2/2-Retro-hSyn-Cre into vPAG (AP −4.52 mm, ML ±0.42 mm, DV 2.78 mm) combined with rAAV-DIO-hM3Dq-EYFP in ZI to label vPAG-projecting ZI neurons.
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Stereotaxic targeting of ZI (AP −1.2 mm, ML ±1.6 mm, DV 4.4 mm) with histological verification by confocal imaging of EGFP signal and DAPI in 40 µm brain sections; bilateral expression required for inclusion.
Photometry Data: Population: ZI neurons expressing GCaMP6s (rAAV-hSyn-GCaMp6s, fiber photometry). Epochs: (1) exploring object—Shock only: no change; Object: increased ΔF/F; (2) burying behavior—increased ΔF/F in both groups; (3) self-grooming—decreased ΔF/F in both groups. N=5 mice per group; statistical test: One-way ANOVA, p<0.001. Peak ΔF/F, latency, and duration not explicitly stated.
Purpose of this circuit: To normalize anxiety-like behavior induced by inescapable stress via ZI→vPAG projections, without altering defensive burying behavior.

Title: Zona Incerta GABAergic Neurons Facilitate Emergence from Isoflurane Anesthesia in Mice.
Authors: Chen H, Liu C, Liu J, Yuan C, He H, Zhang Y, Yu S, Luo T, Shen W, Yu T
Animal Model: VGAT-IRES-Cre mice; C57BL/6J mice
Authors and Publication Year: Hong Chen, Chengxi Liu, Junxiao Liu, Chengdong Yuan, Haifeng He, Yu Zhang, Shouyang Yu, Tianyuan Luo, Wei Shen, Tian Yu; 2024

Title: Inhibitory medial zona incerta pathway drives exploratory behavior by inhibiting glutamatergic cuneiform neurons
Authors: Sandeep Sharma
Animal Model: Mus musculus: vGLUT2-IRES-Cre and vGAT-IRES-Cre transgenic mouse lines
Authors and Publication Year: Sandeep Sharma, Cecilia A. Badenhorst, Donovan M. Ashby, Stephanie A. Di Vito, Michelle A. Tran, Zahra Ghavasieh, Gurleen K. Grewal, Cole R. Belway, Alexander McGirr, Patrick J. Whelan (2024)
Anatomical connections:
1) Retrograde tracing: injection of AAVrg-DIO-ChR2-eYFP into CnF of vGAT-IRES-Cre mice → labeled GABAergic cell bodies in medial zona incerta (mZI) (retrograde AAV).
2) Anterograde tracing: injection of AAV-DJ-hSyn-Flex-mGFP-2A-Synaptophysin-mRuby into mZI of vGAT-IRES-Cre mice → synaptophysin-mRUBY+ puncta in ipsilateral CnF (anterograde AAV).
3) RNAscope: fluorescent in situ hybridization for vGLUT2 mRNA combined with SYP-mRUBY immunolabeling in CnF → majority of SYP-mRUBY+ puncta apposed to vGLUT2+ CnF neurons.
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: Histological verification of viral reporter expression in medial ZI using confocal imaging and alignment to Allen Mouse Brain Atlas; optical fiber tracks confirmed above mZI
Photometry Data:
Population: mZI vGAT neurons
Indicator: GCaMP6s via AAV9-CAG.Flex.GCaMP6s in vGAT-IRES-Cre; bulk fiber photometry
Behavioral epochs and key findings:
• Immobility (hole-board): no significant change vs baseline (p=0.223)
• Rearing onset: increased Ca2+ (paired t-test, t(4)=4.165, p=0.0141)
• Head-dip onset: robust increase (t(4)=19.19, p<0.0001)
• Thigmotactic locomotion onset: decrease in signal (t(4)=4.085, p=0.0150)
• Focused exploration locomotion: increase (t(4)=7.00, p=0.0022)
• Open field locomotion onset: modest decrease (t(4)=3.638, p=0.0222)
N animals: 5 mice
Signal metric: normalized z-score
Statistical test: two-tailed paired t-test
Control signal: 405 nm isosbestic channel
Hardware: Doric fiber photometry system
Figure refs: Fig. 5d–j (main text)
Electrophysiology Data: Bulk extracellular recordings in anesthetized mice; optogenetic activation of mZI vGATChR2 somata (5-pulse, 10 Hz burst) inhibited firing in 7/27 CnF units (26%); no intrinsic electrophysiological properties (Cm, Rin, AP kinetics) were reported
Purpose of this circuit: The mZI→CnF GABAergic circuit promotes exploratory behavior by inhibiting glutamatergic CnF neurons.

Title: Multimodal analysis reveals cellular diversity and divergent circuits of the zona incerta
Authors: Ryan Kast
Animal Model: Mouse (adult wild-type for snRNA-seq; Vgat-IRES-Cre, Nos1-IRES-Cre, Spp1-P2A-Cre, Slc30a3-IRES-Cre lines for circuit tracing, FISH, and electrophysiology)
Authors and Publication Year: Ryan Kasta; Sean K. Simmons; Nita Romea; Xian Adiconis; Lisa Melamed; Kathryn A. McCabe; Dongqing Wang; Alexandra Krol; Magdalena Krubner; Vincent Prevosto; Kirsten Levandowski; Ubadah Sabbagh; Heather A. Sullivan; Ian R. Wickersham; Fan Wang; Joshua Z. Levin; Zhanyan Fu; Guoping Feng (2026)
Anatomical connections: Anterograde: Vgat+ ZI→SC; Vgat+ ZI→PAG; Vgat+ ZI→PRN; Vgat+ ZI→nucleus reuniens, POm, CL, PF; Vgat+ ZI→anterior hypothalamic area; Vgat+ ZI→lateral preoptic area. Retrograde: ZI←RN; ZI←PRN; ZI←GRN (predominantly dorsal ZI/Kcng2+ neurons); ZI←POm; ZI←SC; ZI←dmPAG (predominantly ventral ZI/Pax6+ neurons). Collateralization: ZI-SC and ZI-PRN are segregated. Cell-type anterograde: Slc30a3+ ZI→dmPAG; Slc30a3+, Spp1+ ZI→SC, POm. Dorsal ZI Nos1+ and Spp1+→midbrain/pons. Monosynaptic rabies: inputs to ZI-SCSlc30a3+, ZI-SCSpp1+, ZI-PRNSpp1+, ZI-PRNNos1+.
Verification of Zona Incerta Targeting: RNA FISH of Gad2, Vglut2, and Pax6 across serial sagittal sections; coexpression to delineate ZI boundaries; exclusion of neighboring STN, thalamus, TRN; FANS of NeuN+ nuclei and removal of non-ZI clusters in snRNA-seq.
Photometry Data: Fiber photometry of jGCaMP8m in SC-projecting and PRN-projecting ZI neurons; recordings aligned to lick-bout onset/offset, looming onset, escape onset, freeze onset. ZI-SC: pre-lick increase (AUC P=0.0272), modest bout suppression, activation on escape, strong freeze suppression (P=0.0174). ZI-PRN: no pre-lick increase, suppression during licking (interaction P=0.0415), activation on escape, milder freeze suppression.
Electrophysiology Data: 1) Ventral ZI Slc30a3+: Cm ~85 pF (N=14), Rin ~1.6 GΩ (N=14); slower APs, depolarization blockade. 2) Ventral ZI Spp1+: Cm ~130 pF (N=25), Rin ~0.8 GΩ (N=25); fast APs, minimal adaptation. 3) Dorsal ZI Nos1+: Cm ~90 pF (N=18), Rin ~1.4 GΩ (N=25); depolarization blockade. 4) Dorsal ZI Spp1+: Cm ~110 pF (N=11), Rin ~1.0 GΩ (N=12); fast APs, no blockade.
Purpose of this circuit: To define genetically and anatomically distinct ZI GABAergic neuron subtypes, map their brain-wide inputs and outputs, and determine their functional recruitment during an approach-avoidance conflict between reward consumption and visual threat.
